diffs.diff: magnetic flux density (Gauss, at Vs=5V): datasheet reading gives 714.2857 per count, the part's model has 1082
diffs.evidence: Both readings use the same datasheet sensitivity, evaluated at different supply voltages. Honeywell SS39ET/SS49E/SS59ET product sheet: 'The linear sourcing output voltage is set by the supply voltage and varies in proportion to the strength of the magnetic field'; Sensitivity (25 C) min 1.0 / typ 1.4 / max 1.75 mV/Gauss; Null (0 Gauss) 2.25 / 2.50 / 2.75 Vdc (at Vs=5 V); the 'Sensitivity per Volt (mV/Gauss/V)' vs supply voltage plot shows the output is ratiometric. Second reading at Vs=5 V: 1/0.0014 V/G = 714.29 G/V, offset -2.5 V x 714.29 = -1785.7 G. The model simulates the module powered from 3.3 V, as it recommends for ESP32/Pico ADCs: sensitivity 1.4 mV/G x 3.3/5 = 0.924 mV/G, so 1/0.000924 = 1082 G/V, with null at 1.65 V (sim vAtMin 0.726 V at -1000 G, vAtMax 2.574 V at +1000 G; offset -1785.7 G, which matches the second reading). Ratio 1082/714.29 = 1.515 = 5/3.3, exactly the supply ratio. The driver scales with vcc: sens = 0.0014 x vcc/5, zero = vcc/2, so it gives the 5 V values when vcc=5.0.
